name: MPFB (MakeHuman for Blender)
notes: 2026-11-01: Blender extension generating parametric rigged humans; proposed route is Blender Python in background mode. Rigify ships with Blender and needs no separate record.
2026-11-01: Captured from conversation; listed-in-prd is the schema's listed-only status. Licence, version and maintenance not yet assessed.
2026-11-01: Triage: assess. Concrete job: human figures and character motion, absent from the catalogue.
2026-11-15: MPFB2 release v2.0.18 dated 2026-10-11. Source code is GPLv3; core bundled assets are CC0. Check third-party asset packs separately.

install.macos: Download the MPFB 2.0.18 extension zip from https://extensions.blender.org/download/sha256:c075b3e9b94b8e5556a5f03f4653602d02ea306de08126e8f55ed6dee28a2dad/add-on-mpfb-v2.0.18.zip and check its sha256. Install with blender --factory-startup --command extension install-file -r user_default <zip>, with HOME and BLENDER_USER_* pointed into the example's output/ directory. See examples/mpfb-human-figure/run.sh.

evidence.result: Blender 4.4.0 background: default human at height 0.0/0.5/1.0 has 13380 vertices each, bbox height 1.30/1.66/2.37 m; 480x720 transparent Workbench still; identical geometry across reruns
evidence.scope: Headless Blender 4.4.0 loads MPFB 2.0.18 from an isolated repo, sets height macro, checks geometry and one still; no clothing, rigs, other macros or EEVEE; macOS arm64

source: conversation 2026-11-01: character and figure tooling gap
summary: MakeHuman Community Blender add-on for parameterized human creation and rigging; produces editable Blender characters that can be exported or rendered through Blender.
use_when: When Blender-based parametric human creation is needed
When a rigged editable character is preferable to a runtime avatar
license: GPL-3.0 source; core assets CC0; check third-party packs separately

assessment.rationale: MPFB2 is an open-source Blender human generator; upstream release v2.0.18 is dated 2026-10-11. Source is GPLv3 while core assets are CC0, according to the project license pages. The documented Blender extension workflow is a plausible native authoring route; retain as a candidate.
